number.why: The served arm changes, SDs and denominators are supported and yield an unadjusted MD of -17.4 minutes at 3 weeks. This is a reconstructed difference, not the source-reported ANCOVA estimate of -15.6 minutes (95% CI -25.3 to -6). The latter confidence interval cannot be attached to -17.4. Confirmation applies to the explicitly reconstructed, 3-week result.

entry.why: Agree with the structured lane_ruling ESTABLISHED and its accepted resolution; disagree with the stale PARTLY statement in the narrative. Adults aged 65-80 with primary insomnia satisfy the question's population. Restricting the estimate to this subgroup limits generalizability but does not make eligibility only partly established.

quotes.span: Men and women aged between 18 and 80 years suffering from primary insomnia according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual for Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) criteria with sleep latency longer than 20 min were included in the study.
Pre-planned analysis on ITT population age 65-80

Patients still eligible after the 2-week placebo run-in and who were compliant with respect to treatment, had a negative drug screen and correctly completed study assessment forms were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either PRM 2 mg or placebo for 3 weeks in a double-blind manner.

missed: The reconstruction selection rule's claim of no target published effect is contradicted by the quoted registry ANCOVA result. This requires correcting the selection rationale, although it does not invalidate the arithmetic reconstruction. The generic 'end of treatment' label must specify 3 weeks, as quoted above. The ruling already identifies the analysis-set mismatch and adjusted/unadjusted distinction, but its narrative PARTLY conclusion remains inconsistent with its final ESTABLISHED ruling.
